decisionsTitle: The rain is a raining cloud and a percentage, never a closed umbrella (amending §402, §416, §429)
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-08:** «queue the weather rain icon change, I hate that umbrella closed, show percentages of precipitation as well».

**What was there.** The forecast (§402, §416, §429, §469) drew MUI's `Umbrella` — a closed umbrella — in two roles. (1) As the sky's own glyph for showers and heavy rain: `WEATHER_GLYPH.showers` (`src/modules/weather/ui/glyphs.ts`), to which WMO 65 and 80–82 map (`domain/wmo.ts`). (2) As the «rain likely» marker beside the sky's glyph under §429's rule (`rainLikely`: a chance of 50% or more, or 0.5 mm already falling in the hour, unless the sky says snow, frost or the storm): on a listing card's pill («🌧 ☂ 9 °C»), on the featured hero's «Vremea» line and in the event page's weather row (`weather-rain-likely`). A card's pill said only the glyph and the degrees — «☁ 14 °C» — however likely the rain.

**Decision — no closed umbrella anywhere, two replacements, one per role.**

- **The sky's glyph for showers and heavy rain is a cloud with rain falling from it.** `@mui/icons-material` has no such glyph (its `Shower` is a bathroom's, `BeachAccess` a parasol, `Water` waves), so the project draws one: `src/modules/weather/ui/RainyIcon.tsx`, made with MUI's own `createSvgIcon` (imported from `@mui/material/SvgIcon`, where MUI now exports it; the `@mui/material/utils` re-export is deprecated) from the path of Google's Material Symbols «rainy» glyph, filled, weight 400 — Apache License 2.0, named with its source in the file's comment — rescaled from the Symbols' 960-unit grid to the 24-unit viewBox every Material icon here uses. It is one `<path>`, takes `fontSize` and `color` like every other glyph, reads at 18 px beside the pills, and its test id is «RainyIcon». `WEATHER_GLYPH.showers` points at it; `rain` keeps `WaterDrop`, `drizzle` keeps `Grain`; nothing else in the map moves.
- **The «rain likely» marker is the chance itself, said in figures, with a drop before it.** On a card's pill: «🌧 9 °C 💧 60 %» — `WaterDrop` at 18 px, then the percentage. On the hero's line and the event page's row: the drop instead of the umbrella before the existing words («ploaie probabilă» on the hero, after its «60% șanse de ploaie»; «ploaie probabilă 60 %» on the event page, §469).

**The percentage on every card that has one.** A card's pill (the listing's cards, a series card's next date and the featured hero's pill) shows the hour's chance after the degrees whenever the forecast has one and it does not round to 0 — «☁ 14 °C 💧 20 %». The drop and the figure are in `text.secondary`, like the sky's glyph; when rain is likely (§429) both take the primary colour, so the likely hour stands out without a second glyph — including a likely hour by amount alone at a low chance, since §429's rule decides the colour, not the figure. 0 % — or a chance that rounds to it, or none — shows nothing, except on a likely hour: a dry hour has nothing to read, as §469 said of a tenth of a millimetre. A likely hour with no chance to show — likely by its amount alone (0.5 mm or more) while the forecast has no chance or one that rounds to 0 — still draws the drop, alone and in the primary colour, with no figure: «☁ 9 °C 💧». Without it the eye would get nothing where the umbrella used to stand and the pill's `data-rain-likely` and a screen reader's «ploaie probabilă» say rain is likely; the hero's line and the event page's row already mark that hour with the drop and «ploaie probabilă». A snowy, frosty or stormy hour shows its chance in `text.secondary` and is never «rain likely» (Open-Meteo's chance is of any precipitation). The pill stays 24 px high and one line (`whiteSpace: nowrap`); its widest case, «🌧 −12 °C 💧 100 %», is about 140 px, well inside a 320-px card, and the route's row already wraps.

**The words.** One new key in both catalogues, `Weather.chanceShort`: «{percent} %» / "{percent}%" — the locale's own spacing, the same plain space `Weather.rainLikelyChance` already writes in Romanian (the catalogues carry no no-break space anywhere, and the pill never wraps). `Weather.rainShort` («{percent}% ploaie») was not reused: its word repeats what the drop already says and widens the pill. A screen reader now hears the chance in words after the degrees, as the hero's line says it — «Vremea la start: Înnorat, 12 °C, 20% șanse de ploaie» — exactly when the figure is drawn, then «ploaie probabilă» / "rain likely" when rain is likely, as before.

**What does not change.** §429's rule and threshold (`rainLikely`, 50% or 0.5 mm, never on snow, frost or the storm); the `data-rain-likely` attribute and the spoken «ploaie probabilă» / "rain likely" — what the eye gets changes, what a screen reader hears of the rule does not; the hero's «20% șanse de ploaie» in words; the event page's row as §469 set it (the chance only when rain is likely, as «ploaie probabilă N %»); the reminder email's one line (§469), words only.

**Known, left for the owner.** A plain rain hour (WMO 61 and 63) keeps `WaterDrop` as its sky's glyph, so its pill reads «💧 12 °C 💧 70 %» and the hero's line a drop before «ploaie probabilă» beside a drop as the row's glyph: the same drop in two roles, the second always after the degrees. A different sky glyph for plain rain would tell them apart; it was not asked for here. A snowy, frosty or stormy hour shows its chance with the same drop and a screen reader hears it as «80% șanse de ploaie», as the hero's words already said it: Open-Meteo's chance is of any precipitation, and the sky's own glyph says which.

**Refused.** An open umbrella: `BeachAccess` is a beach parasol — wrong on a mountain race. A weather-icon library: one SVG path is all that is needed, and the platform prefers nothing over a dependency. The percentage in the reminder: its one line stays as §469 set it. Changing the §429 threshold: the owner asked about the glyph and the figure, not the rule.
changelogLine: - **The rain is a raining cloud and a percentage, never a closed umbrella** — showers and heavy rain draw a cloud with rain falling from it (Material Symbols' «rainy», drawn in the project), and every card's weather pill now says the hour's chance of rain after a drop, «☁ 14 °C 💧 20 %», in the primary colour when rain is likely — a likely hour with no chance to show keeps the drop alone; nothing on a dry hour at 0 %. The hero's line and the event page's row show the drop where the umbrella was; the rule, the spoken words and the reminder are unchanged. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: A listing card's weather pill shows, after the degrees, a drop and the hour's chance of rain in the locale's format («20 %» / "20%") whenever the forecast has a chance that does not round to 0, and nothing at 0 % or without one unless rain is likely; the drop and the figure are in the primary colour exactly when the §429 rain-likely rule holds, otherwise in the secondary text colour; a likely hour with no chance to show (likely by its amount alone, with no chance or one that rounds to 0) draws the drop alone, in the primary colour, with no figure; and a screen reader hears the chance in words («20% șanse de ploaie») after the degrees (amending criterion 90; 2026-10-08, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

No weather glyph on a card, the featured hero or the event page is a closed umbrella: showers and heavy rain (WMO 65, 80–82) draw a cloud with rain falling from it (`RainyIcon`), the rain-likely mark on a card is the drop of criterion 90's amendment, and on the hero's line and the event page's row it is a drop before «ploaie probabilă» (amending criteria 90 and 91; 2026-10-08, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

When rain is likely, the event page's weather block and weather row draw a drop, never an umbrella, before «ploaie probabilă» / "rain likely" (on the row «ploaie probabilă N %» / "rain likely N%"); on a dry hour the row still shows no chance (amending criteria 45 and 48; 2026-10-08, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).
